mappings.name: FL25VersionString
mappings.notes: FL 25 emits a NUL-terminated UTF-16LE product-version string under opcode 0x36 — a BYTE-range opcode with a variable-length payload, violating PyFLP's range-based sizing rules. Fork patch in vendor/PyFLP/pyflp/_fl25_overrides.py adds `utf16_zterm` size rule. Regression: tests/test_pyflp_fl25.py::test_fl25_opcode_0x36_decodes_as_one_string_event.

mappings.name: ProjectTempo
mappings.notes: DWORD+28 event carrying bpm × 1000 as a uint32 LE. PyFLP has had this mapped as ProjectID.Tempo for years; confirmed still correct on FL 25 once the 0x36 / 0xC0 overrides realign the event stream. Regression: tests/test_pyflp_fl25.py::test_fl25_tempo_decodes_to_120.

mappings.name: FL25CompoundProjectProperties
mappings.notes: FL 25 stores a compound project-properties blob under what PyFLP legacy-mapped as ChannelID._Name. Contents: tempo, loop mode, time signature, pan law, title-adjacent fields, etc. Fork patch routes this to UnknownDataEvent on FL 25+ to unblock parsing; inner structure not yet decoded (FL re-decomposes into individual events on subsequent saves, so the blob is transient). Regression: tests/test_pyflp_fl25.py::test_fl25_base_fixtures_parse.

mappings.name: PluginStateData
mappings.notes:
DATA+21 event carrying a plugin's internal state blob (VST or native). For VSTs the blob is the plugin's fxChunk; for native plugins it's FL's typed state. PyFLP knows this as PluginID.Data. Verified empirically via a MasterVol sweep on Serum (channel 1 of tests/corpus/re_base/fl25/base_one_serum.flp): the 0xd5 payload is the only non-save-noise opcode that changes when plugin params change. Plugin params ARE scriptable via plugins.setParamValue(value, paramIndex, index, slotIndex) — earlier assumption that GUI automation was required was wrong. Note for Serum specifically: the blob's size varies across saves at the same param values (VST-internal session state), which complicates fixed-offset RE; FL's native plugins (e.g. Fruity Parametric EQ 2) likely have more deterministic serialization.

Fruity Parametric EQ 2 decoder: see `src/flp_diff/plugins/fruity_eq2.py`. Full 36-parameter byte-offset map reverse-engineered 2026-04-17 via plugins.setParamValue sweeps against insert 13 slot 4 of edz_chords_28.flp. Per-band layout: 4-byte slots, uint16 LE for level/freq/width, uint8 for type/order. Main level uint16 LE at 0x90. Round-trip verified against captured sweep blob.

mappings.name: MixerParams
mappings.notes: DATA+33 event carrying a list of (channel_data << 6, slot, msg, ...) mixer parameters. PyFLP knows this as MixerID.Params and decodes it fine, BUT the channel_data bit-packing is sparse on FL 25 — most insert indices don't get populated. Fork patch in vendor/PyFLP/pyflp/mixer.py uses `defaultdict(_InsertItems)` so Insert objects iterate cleanly without KeyError on missing entries. Regression: tests/test_pyflp_fl25.py::test_fl25_mixer_iteration_does_not_keyerror.

mappings.name: TimeSpentSaveCounter
mappings.notes: Observed empirically on 2026-04-17: a scratch-vs-scratch sweep of two saves at the SAME tempo (120 → 120) showed only two opcodes changing — 0xc0 (compound blob, only when still in that form) and 0xf2 (28-byte payload, middle 5 bytes differ between saves). The differing bytes look like a float64 — likely FL's per-session time-spent or save-counter. Probable save-noise; filter from diff signal. Needs triangulation sweep to confirm semantics.
